searches.answer: The latest research papers in AI and ML include "SimCLR" from February 2020, which introduced a simplified framework for contrastive learning, and "Idefics2" from April 2024, which improved OCR capabilities with a simplified architecture. Other notable papers are "Phi 3 Vision" from May 2024, a multimodal model, and "GPT-4.5" from February 2025, which represents advancements in scaling unsupervised learning. From Morgan Stanley, papers include "Rethinking Langevin Thompson Sampling" and "Average-Case Hardness of Parity Problems."
